question: What is the primary setting targeted by the School Health Programme?
explanation: The programme specifically focuses on protecting and promoting health within schools where children spend most of their daytime hours. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why are health and learning considered intertwined in school health philosophy?

options.A: Healthy children achieve better academic outcomes
options.B: Schools get extra funding for running clinics
options.C: Teachers are legally required to give out medications
options.D: Academic tests measure physical fitness levels

explanation: A child must be physically and mentally well to fully engage with and benefit from classroom instruction. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is one of the classic pillars of the school health triad?
explanation: Health instruction, along with health services and healthful school living, forms the foundational triad of school health. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of early detection in school health programmes?

options.A: To catch health issues before they impair learning
options.B: To punish students who break school health rules
options.C: To reduce the number of teachers needed in class
options.D: To generate financial reports for the government

explanation: Finding problems like poor vision or hearing early prevents them from negatively affecting a child's academic progress. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h2)

question: What role does the school nurse commonly play in supporting student mental health?

options.A: Grading students on mental health examinations
options.B: Observing behavioral shifts and listening to concerns

explanation: Nurses are often the first to notice emotional distress and provide a safe listening space or referral when needed. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h3)

question: A student appears unusually quiet, withdraws from peers, and drops in academic performance. What does this situation call for?

options.A: Assessment for potential mental well-being concerns
options.C: Mandatory physical exercise drills after hours
options.D: Restriction from all school feeding programmes

explanation: Sudden behavioral and academic changes are classic red flags for underlying mental or emotional stress in students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which measure is most effective for controlling infectious diseases in a school setting?

options.A: Removing all washing facilities from school grounds
options.B: Banning all outdoor sports activities permanently
options.C: Isolating children in windowless rooms all day
options.D: Promoting proper hand hygiene and immunization checks

explanation: Handwashing and verifying immunization records are proven, frontline defenses against the spread of infections among children. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why must school nurses also focus on non-communicable conditions like asthma?

options.A: Asthma attacks can spread rapidly from child to child
options.B: Children with asthma cannot participate in lessons at all
options.C: Non-communicable diseases are always caused by poor hygiene
options.D: These chronic conditions require daily management at school

explanation: Conditions like asthma require school staff to know emergency protocols, such as administering rescue inhalers when symptoms flare up. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following is a key component of a healthful school physical environment?

options.A: Private lockers for all enrolled students
options.C: Air conditioning in every single room

explanation: Adequate sanitation and clean toilets are non-negotiable requirements for preventing disease transmission in schools. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is regular inspection of school food vendors necessary?

options.A: To force local vendors to close their businesses permanently
options.B: To check that students only eat imported food items
options.C: To ensure the school makes a profit from food sales
options.D: To prevent outbreaks of foodborne illnesses among students

explanation: Unregulated food vendors can sell contaminated meals or drinks, leading to widespread gastroenteritis and waterborne infections. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of health education in schools?

options.A: Training every child to become a professional nurse
options.B: Reducing the budget allocated for school feeding
options.C: Empowering students to make healthy choices independently
options.D: Eliminating the need for any physical education classes

explanation: Health education equips children with the knowledge and attitudes needed to practice healthy habits on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h6)

question: How does school-based health education impact the wider community?

options.A: Parents lose responsibility for teaching their children
options.B: Communities stop building local health clinics entirely
options.C: Local hospitals experience a permanent drop in staffing
options.D: Children take healthy habits home to their families

explanation: Students act as health messengers, sharing hygiene and nutrition practices learned at school with their families at home. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which condition is commonly checked during routine school health screening?
explanation: Vision screening is a standard part of school health checks because poor eyesight directly impacts reading and classroom learning. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the immediate next step after a school nurse identifies a health defect during a screening?

options.A: Providing a prompt referral for further clinical care
options.B: Keeping the finding secret from the parents
options.D: Expelling the student from the school system

explanation: Screening is only useful if followed by a referral so the child can receive proper diagnosis and treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h7)

question: Who must be involved to make a school health programme truly successful?

options.A: External security contractors and police officers
options.B: Only the school principal and government auditors
options.C: Teachers, parents, and local healthcare workers
options.D: Strictly the senior students in the graduating class

explanation: School health is a collaborative effort involving everyone who has a stake in the child's well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h8)

question: Why is parent involvement essential in school health initiatives?

options.A: To pay salaries for the school health staff
options.B: To reinforce healthy behaviors at home
options.C: To take over daily nursing duties in class
options.D: To design the academic curriculum for the term

explanation: When parents support health lessons at home, children receive consistent messages that make healthy habits stick. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h8)
